\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{सद्यः} (sadyaḥ)}{सद्यः (sadyaḥ)}]{\sk{सद्यः} (sadyaḥ) — at once}

\label{lesson:SA-C213-sadyah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a dream, then the Sanskrit for satisfaction.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{सद्यः}}
\textbf{\sk{सद्यः}} — \emph{sadyaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}at once\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sadyaḥ} is built on \emph{sa-}, \textquotedblleft{}same\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{dyu}, \textquotedblleft{}day\textquotedblright{} (MW; CDIAL 13123): \textquotedblleft{}on the same day\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}at once\textquotedblright{}. It is already in the Rigveda.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sadyaḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{sadyaḥ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for a dream, then the Sanskrit for satisfaction, then say \emph{sadyaḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{तत्क्षणम्} (tatkṣaṇam)}{तत्क्षणम् (tatkṣaṇam)}]{\sk{तत्क्षणम्} (tatkṣaṇam) — instantly}

\textbf{\sk{तत्क्षणम्}} — \emph{tatkṣaṇam} — \textquotedblleft{}instantly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tatkṣaṇam} is built on \emph{tat}, \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{kṣaṇa}, \textquotedblleft{}moment\textquotedblright{} (MW): \textquotedblleft{}at that very moment\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL 5640 traces Hindi \emph{takhan}, \textquotedblleft{}then\textquotedblright{}, to it, and CDIAL 3642 links \emph{kṣaṇa} to \emph{akṣi}, \textquotedblleft{}eye\textquotedblright{}, as the twinkling of an eye.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{प्राक्} (prāk)}{प्राक् (prāk)}]{\sk{प्राक्} (prāk) — formerly, before}

\label{lesson:SA-C213-prak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for at once, then the Sanskrit for instantly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{प्राक्}}
\textbf{\sk{प्राक्}} — \emph{prāk} — \textquotedblleft{}formerly, before\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{prāk} is a form of \emph{prāñc}, \textquotedblleft{}turned forward, facing\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{pra}, \textquotedblleft{}forth\textquotedblright{}, and √añc, \textquotedblleft{}to bend, turn\textquotedblright{} (MW). What lies forward is \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{} in time and, facing the sunrise, the east.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{अनन्तरम्} (anantaram)}{अनन्तरम् (anantaram)}]{\sk{अनन्तरम्} (anantaram) — afterwards, next}

\label{lesson:SA-C213-anantaram}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for instantly, then the Sanskrit for formerly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{अनन्तरम्}}
\textbf{\sk{अनन्तरम्}} — \emph{anantaram} — \textquotedblleft{}afterwards, next\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{anantaram} is built on \emph{an-}, \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{antara}, \textquotedblleft{}interval\textquotedblright{} (MW): \textquotedblleft{}with no interval\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}immediately after\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 287). CDIAL lists Marathi \emph{nãtar}, \textquotedblleft{}afterwards\textquotedblright{}, under it, asking whether Marathi took it from Sanskrit.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{यावत्} (yāvat)}{यावत् (yāvat)}]{\sk{यावत्} (yāvat) — as long as, until}

\label{lesson:SA-C213-yavat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for formerly, then the Sanskrit for afterwards.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{यावत्}}
\textbf{\sk{यावत्}} — \emph{yāvat} — \textquotedblleft{}as long as, until\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{yāvat} is built on the relative stem \emph{ya-}, \textquotedblleft{}which\textquotedblright{} (MW), and MW pairs it with its correlative \emph{tāvat}, \textquotedblleft{}so long\textquotedblright{}. It is a Rigvedic word for \textquotedblleft{}as long as, until\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10474).
\end{cousinweb}
